title: Anaphylaxis - rebound after auto-injector
objectives: Repeat epi 0.3 mg IM (1 mg/mL) without delay
IV + NS bolus for hypotension (MAP >= 65 / SBP >= 90)
Intercept vs. direct to UVMMC (18 min); epi re-dose plan en route
resources: Epi 1 mg/mL + syringes / auto-injectors, IV, NS 2 L, DuoNeb, O2, BVM, suction. UVMMC ~18 min. Paramedic intercept ETA: ______
dispatch: UVM Rescue, respond to Camp Birchwood, 300 Lakeshore Dr (Malletts Bay), for a 29-year-old male, allergic reaction, difficulty breathing. Camp nurse on scene. Time out 1410.

scene.location: Camp health lodge cot. 82 F, humid. Gravel camp road; UVMMC ~18 min.
scene.setup: Pt seated on cot edge, scratching. Used EpiPen trainer on table. Camp nurse present.
scene.moulage: Red marker blotches (hives) on neck/chest/arms; sting site L forearm.
scene.roles: Pt actor; camp nurse (gave EpiPen 0.3 mg at 1358, ~14 min before contact).

patient.name: Tyler Morin
patient.on_arrival: Sitting upright, flushed with hives, hoarse 2-3 word answers, audible wheeze, anxious.

SAMPLE: Throat tight, itchy, SOB, lightheaded, nauseated, 1x vomit
Stung L forearm ~1355 clearing brush; nurse gave EpiPen 1358, "got better then came back"
OPQRST: Worse lying back? No - worse sitting up (dizzy)
Improved ~5 min after EpiPen, worse again past ~5 min

primary: Patent, **hoarse voice**, lip/uvula swelling, no stridor yet
RR 28, accessory use, diffuse expiratory wheeze
Radial weak, rapid. Skin flushed, warm, hives
Generalized urticaria; stinger visible L forearm
**HIGH**: anaphylaxis w/ airway + resp + shock signs. Epi now
secondary: Sting site, stinger in place (scrape off)

vitals.other: Wheeze, hoarse, hives. Sinus tach. Shark-fin capno
Voice clearer, wheeze less, hives fading
Throat tight again, hoarse. -> epi #3 (max 3; MD for more)

vitals.trigger: IF no epi by T+5 OR pt stood up

flow.give: Nurse: "I gave his EpiPen at 1358, he got better, now it's back." Stage **A**.
expected: Roles: one on epi, one on airway/O2

branches.if: Diphenhydramine/neb first, or epi delayed > T+5

branches.then: partner catches if asked; critical (evaluator discretion)

expected: Epi 0.3 mg IM (1 mg/mL) anterolateral thigh
Pt laid supine, legs flat, not walked

flow.give: Pt's veins good. Stinger still in skin if crew looks.
expected: IV large bore; NS bolus (up to 30 mL/kg) to SBP >= 90

branches.then: Stage **E** airway signs; expect epi re-dose, BVM/suction ready, MD + intercept

branches.if: Pt allowed to walk / sit up

expected: Direct to UVMMC vs. intercept decided (no scene delay)

flow.give: Stage **D** at ~T+22. Pt: "It's coming back, my throat..."

branches.then: MD contact for epi beyond 3 doses; airway equipment ready

flow.give: Evaluator plays medic intercept or ED.
expected: Handoff: times of all 3 epi doses, fluid total

critical: Epi not given within 5 min of contact
Wrong epi concentration/route (0.1 mg/mL IM or 1 mg/mL IV)
No IV fluid for SBP < 90 after epi
Failure to re-dose epi for recurrence
differentials: Known allergen, hives, wheeze, hoarse, hypotension
debrief: Why did symptoms return 15-20 min after the auto-injector?
Why supine, and why did standing make him crash?
Epi before everything - why are antihistamines second line?
How did you decide intercept vs. go direct with UVMMC 18 min away?
How do you avoid an epi concentration error under stress?

crew_card.dispatch: Camp Birchwood, 300 Lakeshore Dr (Malletts Bay). 29 y/o M, allergic reaction, difficulty breathing. Camp nurse on scene.
crew_card.on_arrival: Health lodge. Young man sitting on cot, red blotches, scratching, hoarse, breathing hard. Nurse holding a used EpiPen.

actor_card.Act: Anxious, scratch constantly, hoarse 2-3 word answers. Say you're dizzy sitting up.
actor_card.After epi: Within ~3 min voice gets better, breathe easier.
actor_card.If you stand / walk: Sway, "I'm gonna pass out", sit/collapse to ground.
actor_card.~T+22: "It's coming back... my throat" - hoarse again.
actor_card.If no epi by T+5: Make high-pitched noise breathing in (stridor), very drowsy.

show_cards.title: SKIN / FACE
show_cards.body:
Raised red welts neck, chest, arms, back.
Lips swollen. Uvula swollen.

show_cards.title: LUNG SOUNDS
show_cards.body:
Diffuse expiratory wheezes, all fields.
Diminished at bases.

moulage_tags.text: Lips swollen. Uvula swollen. Voice hoarse
Sting site - stinger still in skin
Wheezes all fields, diminished at bases
